I don't have a shell tool available in this session to execute `npm test`, so I'll verify the fix by inspection instead.

The change to `src/domain/lifecycle.ts:139` now rejects `releaseTask` on a `cancelled` task with `Task ${taskId} is already cancelled, nothing to release`, before any DB mutation happens — so the status/owner/lock/reason are all left untouched. `claimTask` and `cancelTask` are unmodified, and the normal pending/in_progress release path (the two tests above it) is untouched since that branch only changed its trigger condition, not its logic.

**Root cause:** `releaseTask` only guarded against releasing a `done` task, not a `cancelled` one. Since `cancelTask` clears `owner_session_id`/`lock_expires_at` (so there's no active lock to trip the conflict check) but leaves `cancellation_reason` set, a later `release_task` call on that same task ID — e.g. a stale client retry, or an orchestrator that doesn't realize the task was cancelled out from under it — would silently flip it back to `pending` with no error, and `get_next_task` would then hand it out again, exactly matching the report (cancellation reason still present, cancelled state gone, no error, no logs).

**Fix:** `releaseTask` now rejects with `Task X is already cancelled, nothing to release` the same way it already does for `done`, added a regression test in `tests/lifecycle.test.ts` covering it, without touching `claimTask`, `cancelTask`, or normal release behavior.

Only one write path resets to `pending`, confirming this is the sole culprit. The fix is complete.

**Root cause:** `releaseTask` (`src/domain/lifecycle.ts`) only rejected releasing a `done` task, never checked for `cancelled`. Since `cancelTask` clears `owner_session_id`/`lock_expires_at`, a later stray `release_task` call (e.g. a worker that claimed the task before someone else cancelled it, calling release afterward) skips the ownership-conflict check entirely and falls through to the unconditional `UPDATE ... SET status = 'pending'`, silently reviving the cancelled task while `cancellation_reason` stays stale from the earlier cancellation — exactly the symptom reported, with no error since the existing guard only names `done`.

**Fix:** extended the existing guard to also reject `cancelled` tasks (`throw Error("Task X is already cancelled, nothing to release")`), mirroring the `done` case exactly — claiming, cancelling, and releasing a normal in-progress task are all untouched. Added a regression test covering claim → cancel → stale release.
